title: One Login to Rule Them All: Cross-App Access for MCP — Garrett Galow, WorkOS
talk_summary: Garrett Galow explains WorkOS's cross-app access (XAA) built on the ID-JAG spec, letting an identity provider broker short-lived MCP access tokens between a client and server without repeated consent screens. The mechanism is a refresh/ID token exchanged at the IdP for an ID-JAG JWT, which the MCP server validates to issue a normal short-lived OAuth access token.

takeaways.technique: Short-lived brokered tokens instead of standing credentials
takeaways.what_they_do: Access tokens are ~5 minutes and re-minted automatically from the SSO session via the ID-JAG exchange, so revoking the IdP session cuts off access once the token expires.
takeaways.evidence_quote: most applications issue access tokens around 5 minutes... as long as your SSO session is active, you can keep getting these ID Jag tokens

takeaways.technique: Central IdP as trust broker for agent-to-service access
takeaways.what_they_do: The IdP holds the policy of which client may request access to which resource (audience), so access is granted without per-tool consent and is centrally revocable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the identity provider can act as a stand-in, a trust provider between applications

takeaways.what_they_do: The client names the target audience (e.g., mcp.figma.com) and the IdP checks it is allowed to issue for that audience; the server validates the JWT against the IdP.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the MCP client know the app it's requesting access for in Octa? ... based like an audience URL
